o1.biggest_strength: It follows the strongest business signals: much more sleep content, narrator audio as the core format, evening posting, and a clear stop list for quote cards, app news, focus/productivity and morning posts.
o1.biggest_mistake: It over-applies review to all sleep content, so week 1 becomes all kindness and misses the chance to post non-condition wind-down content right away. It also gets the earliest review timing a bit too conservative.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Use week 1 for sleep/wind-down posts that avoid naming conditions, keep narrator clips central, and tighten the review plan so only posts that mention conditions go through clinical/legal review.

o2.biggest_strength: The drafts feel warm, simple and on-brand, and it uses customer language well, especially the email replay, pickup and day-three drop-off moments.
o2.biggest_mistake: The plan does not push sleep hard enough given the install data, keeps a weekly stress-at-work slot, and has a review/calendar conflict around week 2 Monday if those posts need approval.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Shift more of the mix from stress/kindness into sleep narrator clips, give a clearer 4-week calendar with specific post angles, and make the review timing airtight.

reason: I would rather act on Output 1 because it is more complete as a 4-week operating plan and follows the biggest data signals more aggressively. Output 2 has lovely week-1 drafts, but it leaves more performance on the table.
